context:
Goal: remove a false alarm in the guard tests without opening a hole.
Problem (rule): the fix uses Python names that do not exist on Python 3.9, so on 3.9 the guard lets a script write into the guard tests that main refuses, and only you can restart a held change.
Based on (measured): the round-3 reviewer ran 21 cases on the change and on main, simulating Python 3.9, and found the change less safe than main.
Departs from: main holds the change with no work — option a restarts it in one fix lane.
home: step guard-false-alarm-cull (cull guards that cry wolf)

lastAnswer.note: Owner in coordinator chat, 13:31 CST Nov 12, relayed 13:32 CST: one fix lane, review starting over at round 1, makes the new code safe on 3.9 and adds a 3.9 test case.

options.gain: The false alarm goes, and the 3.9 hole is closed.
options.how: One fix lane starts again at review round 1: it guards the three new Python names so 3.9 skips them, and adds a 3.9 test case.
options.label: Restart it in one fix lane (Recommended)

options.how: The held part is dropped; the lane keeps its other fixes.
options.label: Drop this fix

title: Restart the held fix for one guard false alarm, or drop it
why: Only you restart a change held after its third review round.
